Clarinetist Allen Vache was born in New Jersey and currently makes his home in Orlando, Florida. He credits Kenny Davern as an important early influence, as well as his musical family. Allen appears frequently at jazz festivals and concerts here and abroad and his playing is well represented on recordings with the Jim Cullum Jazz Band and as a leader on the Audiophile and Nagel- Heyer Labels.
Allen was interviewed in Scottsdale, Arizona on April 15, 2000, by Monk Rowe, director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
We are in Scottsdale, Arizona. My name is Monk Rowe and we’re filming for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive. I’m very pleased to have Allen Vache with me today, who is a mean clarinet player.
Well I don’t know if it’s “mean.”
I heard you doing some mean bending of notes in that last set that I thought was very interesting.
Yeah with it’s, stylistically, things borrowed from other people. I studied with Kenny Davern when I was in college, and he is one of the masters of the note benders, let’s put it that way.
He’s almost the standard of how people get measured these days.
As far as contemporary jazz players. Whatever possessed you to try and make this a living?
